status: retrospective mechanism audit on spent development products; no holdout claim
question: Can any regular, unique, static local first-gradient completion F(Y,Z,U) distinguish spherical galaxy and cluster points that have the same baryonic surface acceleration?

scope.included: shift-symmetric local quasistatic actions built only from Y=S.S, Z=J.J, and U=S.J, with one physical metric and universal boundary conditions
excluded: curvature, Hessian, density, pressure, or matter-kinematic invariants
object-dependent integration constants or branch choices

decision_rule.close_lane: Close the regular local F(Y,Z,U) lane if at least 95% of cluster points lie within the spent SPARC gbar range, median nearest separation is at most 0.01 dex, median 10-neighbor required-enhancement gap is at least 0.3 dex, and at least 90% of nearest gaps exceed 0.2 dex.
decision_rule.interpretation: The numerical score is retrospective and uses NFW-deprojected cluster accelerations. The structural theorem is exact under its stated assumptions; the score shows that the current development target violates the theorem's universal-RAR consequence.
decision_rule.no_branch_escape: A different branch or integration charge for each object is a forbidden hidden halo state unless a universal baryon-forced boundary law uniquely predicts it.
decision_rule.successor: Require an explicit nonlocal/tidal/source-state variable that distinguishes equal-gbar systems and can transport two-dimensional shear.
